Hi Alex / Blake,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the top priorities. Per our discussion, here’s a short recap and the proposed POC plan so we can lock timelines and owners. Please reply with any edits.

Summary / success criteria (you confirmed these as priority):
- 90th p95 latency under 400ms for single-user queries with 2k token context using a medium model (redwood-bert-2b).
- End-to-end accuracy baseline: intent extraction F1 >= 0.86 on your 250-sample eval set.
- Stability: no more than 2% error rate (timeouts/502s) over 48h of sustained testing.

POC scope and timeline (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria doc and identify technical owner (ACME) + Redwood SE lead.
2) Week 1: SDK integration and sample queries; basic inference + streaming test.
3) Week 2: Run evaluation set, capture latency & token costs; iterate on prompts/quantization.
4) Week 3: Stability test and runback with your product team; decision meeting for next steps.

Owners:
- ACME technical lead: Blake Nguyen (you suggested Blake on the call)
- Redwood SE: Rishi Malhotra (cc'd) — will own SDK integration + test harness
- Redwood Sales (me): project coordination, timeline and procurement touchpoints

Integration notes (technical ask from call):
- We’ll provide the Redwood SDK (Python/Node) and example for streaming token-by-token responses and function/tool calling for your downstream orchestration.
- Primary integration paths: REST generate -> streaming websocket for UI; and SDK-based tool calling for slot-fill workflows.
- We recommend starting with the hosted sandbox keys; if you need private VPC access we can scope Dedicated in parallel.

Attachments: ACME_POC_Success_Criteria.docx (draft) and Redwood_Integration_Guide.pdf (SDK quickstart).

Next steps
- Blake: confirm the technical owner + preferred test environment (staging or dev).
- Alex: confirm the 250-sample eval set delivery date (we discussed Fri EOD).
- Rishi: can you take point on SDK support and a quick walkthrough on Thursday?

Thanks — I’ll update the doc with any feedback after this thread.

Best,
Marissa

Alex — thanks for the quick reply. Blake — great to meet you.

Quick technical plan + integration checklist (Rishi / Dev copied to scope effort):

1) Keys & sandbox
- We’ll provision a limited sandbox API key for your staging cluster. No billing until you flip to production.

2) SDK + sample app
- Redwood SDKs: Python and Node examples included in the attached Integration Guide.
- Endpoints to use: POST /v1/generate for non-streaming; websocket /v1/stream for streaming responses.
- Recommended params: max_tokens=1200, temperature=0.0 for extraction tasks; set stop tokens as needed.

3) Streaming + tool calling
- Streaming: uses a websocket that yields delta tokens; good for low-latency UI updates. Example in the guide shows how to resume on reconnect and handle partial outputs.
- Tool calling: Redwood supports structured function calls — you define tool schemas and the model returns a call which your runtime executes. We’ll share an example for slot-fill and confirmations.

4) Eval harness & metrics
- Rishi will provide a small test harness that runs your 250-sample set against the POC endpoint and captures latency, token counts, and top-line accuracy metrics.

5) Security / network
- If your staging is behind strict egress rules, we can provide a private VPC tunnel or a relay IP list for allowlisting.

6) Support & runbook
- Rishi: 2x 1-hour pair sessions (SDK + streaming walkthrough) the first week; ongoing async slack support.

Estimated time: 3-5 engineering days from Redwood (split across Rishi + Dev), plus your internal setup time.

Next concrete steps:
- Blake: send staging test environment details and confirm firewall/egress constraints.
- Alex: share eval JSONL link by Fri EOD.
- Rishi / Dev: confirm availability for walkthroughs (Rishi, can you do Thu 10am PT?).

I’ll update the success criteria doc after Blake/ Alex confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
